newsitem.title: BELARUS: Thousands hail Lukashenko in Belarus May Day rally.
newsitem.headline: Thousands hail Lukashenko in Belarus May Day rally.

text.p: More than 20,000 people carrying portraits of President Alexander Lukashenko and hardline communists with portraits of Josef Stalin marched side by side through the capital of Belarus to mark May Day on Thursday, while the leader of an opposition protest was arrested.
"Long live the Soviet Union!" read some of the banners in a sea of red hammer and sickle flags and official red and green Soviet-style Belarussian flags re-introduced by Lukashenko.

Belarus gained independence like its neighbours when the Soviet Union fell apart in 1991, but Lukashenko, appealing to nostalgia among the population of 10 million, has signed a Union Treaty with Russia and wants even closer ties with the Kremlin.
The mayor's office had announced the time and place of the rallies in state media and people marched quietly in lines.
At one point portraits of Lukashenko, Soviet founding father Vladimir Lenin and dictator Josef Stalin were held side by side.
Banners bore names of districts and factories in Belarus, which borders Russia, Ukraine, Poland, Lithuania and Latvia.
Opposition newspapers said "quotas" had been allotted saying how many people should attend the rally, which was subdued compared to a smaller protest by Lukashenko's opponents.
They quoted factory workers as saying they had been promised 100,000 Belarussian roubles (about four dollars) for attending.

About 5,000 nationalists marched separately and joined a meeting with the communists and presidential supporters on Independence Square where Nikolai Statkevich, head of the Social Democratic Party in Belarus, addressed the peaceful meeting.
"We will not participate in this show. All of you who were forced to attend please follow me," he said.
A spokesman for the party said Statkevich was later detained for violating a decree by Lukashenko on unsanctioned rallies.

In recent months authorities have restricted street protests which have sometimes erupted in violence with injuries among police and protesters. Hundreds of demonstrators, journalists and bystanders have been detained though mostly for a few hours.

The nationalists, waving red and white flags replaced by Lukashenko with red and green ones following a referendum in May 1995, marched off behind Statkevich to a separate meeting chanting "Down with Luka!" and "Independence!".
Former farm boss Lukashenko won the first presidential election on an anti-corruption drive and has imposed increasingly authoritarian rule.
